details: For finite classes, this is the metric inequality $B(\mathcal H)\ge D(\mathcal H)/2$. Its coefficient $1/2$ is sharp: for the two antipodal concepts $\{\emptyset,[n]\}$ with even $n$, the established values are $B=n/2$ and $D=n$ (database values 77 and 78). Nevertheless there can be no strict endpoint witness $B>D$, since relationship 146 proves $D\ge B$. Equality in the scaled bound is a sharpness example, not a separation witness.
name: Hamming Radius / Diameter
